Hacking your AA MagLite with a holiday decoration LED bulb
Impressive, but not cool until I can change the colors!
Cool but this post is missing the why. What difference does this make?

The original xenon bulbs that come with the Maglite are utter garbage. They aren't bright, they tear through battery life, and they can burn out.

An LED is generally brighter, less power intensive (batteries last longer), and has general life expectancy that's much longer than other types of bulbs.

This. I burned through 2 bulbs before I stopped using my maglite. I just happened to have these leftover bulbs from Christmas decorations and it worked perfectly. I left it on overnight and it was still on the next day.

The only problem I can think of is that you can't connect an LED directly to a voltage source like this. You could damage the batteries or the LED.

Since an LED is a diode, connection without some form of resistance can produce and "infinite current" situation, which isn't good for anything in the circuit. This is why LED options for the Maglite are more than just a bulb, and Maglite PRO LED models are longer than their equivalent standard models. The body of both lights are exactly the same, but the head is longer due to some circuitry used to moderate the voltage.

If you didn't care about any of that, you could probably just use standard prototyping LED indicator bulbs, which would be cheaper and easier to work with. You can get them in packs, and you don't have to disassemble anything.
Nice emergency hack. If you don't have an emergency, thoguh, IMHO you're better off just buying the led Upgrade kit. You can find them from Mag-lite and others for about USD$10.
